definition: ACID names the four properties of a reliable transaction: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. Atomicity makes the group all-or-nothing. Consistency means committed data satisfies the database's constraints. Isolation limits how concurrent transactions see each other. Durability means a committed write survives a crash.
details: Consistency here means constraints, not the distributed-systems meaning of 'every replica agrees'. Those are different words that share a spelling.
examples: A transfer that cannot leave only one account changed
A commit that is still present after the database restarts
